# P03 Regulatory Gap Analysis: Cris Santos Company | Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction | Enterprise: Crude oil producer

| | |

| Scope at this tier | All applicable regulations across the enterprise |
| Expected depth | Requirement-level; evidence sampling; regulator-ready |

| Universal method | [step-05_P03_regulatory-gap-analysis/README.md](../../../../00_universal-framework/projects/step-05_P03_regulatory-gap-analysis/README.md) |
| Scenario brief | [README.md](../README.md) |

**Regulation to analyze:** NIST CSF 2.0 with NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (voluntary benchmark), NIST CSWP 29; NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3
**Why:** Cris Santos Company is an onshore producer here. Per the sector research, onshore-only producers without TSA-designated assets have no binding federal sector cyber rule and should benchmark against NIST CSF 2.0 and NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (OT security). If the company operates Outer Continental Shelf facilities, use the USCG Marine Transportation System cyber rule (N21-R01) instead.

## Regulatory drivers to trace in this deliverable
Use these IDs in the `regulatory_driver` columns of the working files.

| ID | Requirement | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| N21-R01 | USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System final rule | 33 CFR Part 101, Subpart F (33 CFR 101.600-101.670); FR Doc. 2025-00708 (Jan. 17, 2025) |
| N21-R02 | TSA Security Directive Pipeline-2021-02G (Pipeline Cybersecurity Mitigation Actions, Contingency Planning, and Testing) | TSA SD Pipeline-2021-02G, issued under 49 U.S.C. 114 |
| N21-R03 | CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022) - proposed 6 CFR Part 226 | 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (NPRM 89 FR 23644, Apr. 4, 2024) |
